title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 released (Oct 7) — fastest Claude, ~75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5
bullets.summary: Anthropic's third Claude 5.5 release in about a month; built for high-volume, cost-sensitive work and as a subagent alongside Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. Claude Code 2.1.293 already makes it the default Haiku model on the Anthropic API with a 1M context window (per Releasebot's tracker).
bullets.how: The Construct: route classification, summaries, and subagent/swarm worker tasks to Haiku 5.5 to cut cost and latency. Brand 9 Signs: cheap bulk tasks like alt-text, lead triage, and quote classification. PRAGMA: sharpens the model-tiering cost story for client builds.

bullets.title: Claude Code 2.1.289–2.1.293 — Agent-tool effort param, plugin install --marketplace, MCP leak fix
bullets.summary: Releasebot's tracker (first-seen dates Oct 4–7, not confirmed release dates) lists an effort parameter for the Agent tool, claude plugin install --marketplace, a memory-leak fix in HTTP MCP connections, a 529 retry-delay setting, and a fix for file reads from network paths bypassing the permission prompt.
bullets.how: The Construct: set per-subagent effort in swarm runs, and pick up the MCP-connection leak and permission-bypass fixes. PRAGMA: plugin marketplace install is a cleaner client-delivery path. Brand 9 Signs: no direct use.

bullets.title: Mistral Large 4 public preview (Oct 6) — ~1T-param MoE, 1M context, open weights planned end of October
bullets.summary: Per LLM Stats, a ~1.05T total / 52B active MoE with text+image input, 1M context, promo pricing of $0.68 in / $2.09 out per 1M tokens, aimed at coding and agentic tasks; benchmark figures are self-reported and unverified, and the weights license is TBD.
bullets.how: The Construct: candidate low-cost fallback/second-opinion model once weights drop. PRAGMA: possible self-host option for privacy-sensitive clients. Brand 9 Signs: no direct use.

praxis_lesson: Model tiers are now a routing problem, not a pick-one problem: with Haiku 5.5 landing a month after Opus/Sonnet 5.5, assign each agent step the cheapest model (and effort level) that passes its check instead of defaulting everything to the top tier.
